name: Guinea-Bissau
firstCriterion: memorability: a place word people already use plus a short number, unique in the whole country on its own; getting your code takes no effort

verdict.postcodes: paper only: UPU 4-digit format (03/2005), only 1000 and 1011 BISSAU attested; no directory, no use
verdict.doorLevelSystem: none, official or private; 2 house numbers in OpenStreetMap nationwide
verdict.officialAddressAreas: none confirmed; central Bissau has official street names (mixed area, door numbers unverified)

states.official: government address shown first, exactly as written; the N-Ways code beside it
states.mixed: official street + door number shown first where the gate carries one; every gate has its N-Ways code

coverageMask.update: grows towards official when the Câmara Municipal de Bissau, Correios or a national programme publishes or confirms numbering; never shrinks

mixed: bissau-centro: Bissau Velho, Praça/Plateau and central avenues

levels: region (8 + Setor Autónomo de Bissau; not in the code: too large and run by appointed governors)
sector (38 + Bissau = 39; first two digits of the machine form)
place word (bairro in Bissau, town or tabanca elsewhere; what people remember)
compound (morança / quintal / walled plot / institution; the addressable unit)
structure (house, annex, shop in the wall; .k)
hierarchy.sectorNumbering: first digit = region (1 Bissau, 2 Bafatá, 3 Bolama, 4 Biombo, 5 Cacheu, 6 Gabú, 7 Oio, 8 Quinara, 9 Tombali), second = sector alphabetically; 11-19 reserved for Bissau

examples: Malam Baio 15 (official name Sinchã Malam Baio)
remembered.uniqueness: nationally unique on its own: no town, sector, island or phone position is needed; same-named places draw from one national range per name (numbering.nameRanges)

plateName.rule: the place word is the area's plate name: at most 12 characters (letters, spaces, hyphens, apostrophes; an accented letter counts one) and at most 2 words (de/da/do... do not count; a hyphen separates words); no digits
plateName.officialName: kept in model/places.json (officialName), printed small on cards and plates when it differs; never needed; typed, it decodes when it points to one plate name (alias)
plateName.derivation: tools/gw_plates.py with engine/reference/plate_names.py: documented short form (none asserted yet); clean (Bairro de/Tabanca de/Morança, leading Tabanca, brackets, after slash, generic words); as is if it fits; saint-prefix abbreviation (Sto, Sta, S.); else the most distinctive one or two whole words, preferring the end of the name

countryWords.qualifiers: peoples a tabanca is named after (Balanta, Mancanha, Papel, Fula, Mandinga, Beafada, Nalu, Manjaco, Felupe, Bijagó ...), number words, generic words
countryWords.avoid: 38 sector seats, 8 region capitals, Bissau, big cities of the region; the area's own sector seat allowed

plateName.council: needsCouncilChoice + plateCandidates (<= 3) + plateReason when no clear choice, a qualifier or the end of the name would be dropped, only a founder's given name would be left, the short form equals a well-known town, or the name has a number; the first candidate is provisional; codes in a flagged area are issued with the first candidate, and the choice of the Câmara Municipal (Bissau) or the sector administration with the régulos changes the word, never the number
plateName.engine: check_plate refuses a word over the limit; allocate refuses it for an area not flagged for the council and places flagged areas after the confirmed areas of their name

examples.Bambadinca Balanta: council (Bambadinca is a sector seat; Balanta a qualifier)

format.mapping: remembered, written and machine forms map 1:1 through model/places.json and model/name-ranges.json; people remember only the place word and the number
format.alphabet: digits 0-9 only; place words are plate names in their usual Portuguese/Kriol spelling, matched by name key (accents, case, articles, plate abbreviations and spelling variants folded) and aliases (official names included)

checkDigit.over: the name's national number (5 digits), then the compound number (5 digits), then the structure
checkDigit.bindsArea: a code is valid only if the frozen block table gives that number of that name to that area; the area is not a Damm input, so the Damm property covers every digit of the number
checkDigit.catches: with the check digit sent by a system: every single wrong digit and every adjacent swap in the number or check, including those landing in another area of the same name; machine form: the same in NNNNN and C, and every wrong SS-PPP digit landing in another same-named area or nowhere (3.0 % of wrong SS-PPP digits land on a differently named area, whose word is shown)
checkDigit.where: machine form only: forms, partner systems, links, the QR code on the plate; never shown to people

written.where: the remembered form as printed on the plate, in every share and on paper; no check digit

numbering.order: Hilbert curve (order 14) over the sector's spot grid, inside each area's block; land masses kept apart
numbering.growth: even numbers between neighbours; then highest + 1 inside the block; a full block gets a continuation block from the name's spare space

bissau.maxDigits: 4 for every confirmed plate name; 5 for 2 flagged areas (Bambadinca Balanta, Cuntum Madina) whose provisional plate names belong to bigger areas
bissau.sharedNames: 10 of 49 place words share a name; every confirmed one is the largest area of its name, so Bissau's numbers are unchanged

outsideBissau.typicalDigits: 2 (1,492 places) or 3 (1,219 places); 4 in 278; 5 in 23 (21 small places sharing a name with a big town, 2 flagged)

nameRanges.rule: every area (place word, or sector word for index 000) with the same name key draws from ONE national range for that name, 1-99,999, cut into frozen blocks; 'Name NNNNN' decodes to exactly one area and compound anywhere in the country
nameRanges.nameKey: lowercase; ç→s; accents dropped; non-letters→space; 'Bairro/Tabanca/Aldeia/Povoação/Morança (de/da/do)' prefix dropped; plate abbreviations expanded (s.→são, sto→santo, sta→santa, n. sra→nossa senhora); a trailing numeral I-X/1-10 kept as a Roman numeral; small words de da do dos das e o a os as dropped; spelling folds: final que→k, tch ch sh→x, ck qu→k, gu→g, ph→f, nh→n, lh→l, c(e,i)→s, c→k, z→s, y→i, w→u, h dropped, e→i, o→u, doubled letters single; tokens joined
nameRanges.blockSize: smallest of 10, 20, 50, 100 ... 100000 that is >= 4 x the area's compounds at first issue
nameRanges.allocation: per name, areas with a confirmed plate name first, then areas flagged for the council, each by compounds descending; each block starts at the name's high-water mark rounded up to 10^(digits(size)-1)
nameRanges.stability: blocks frozen at issue, never renumbered, moved or shrunk; a new area with an existing name, or a full block, takes the next block above the name's high-water mark
nameRanges.sameSector: two places of one name in one sector are two areas with two blocks; no Roman numeral is invented (that alternative would have created 297 numerals nobody says)
nameRanges.extraParts: the island ('Ambeduco 23 · Orango') and the sector shown beside a code are labels only, never needed to decode
nameRanges.replaces: a context rule (sector shown beside a repeated word, nearer place first), rejected because a code that depends on context fails when it is passed on

qualifiers.rule: if a name's blocks would pass 99,999: one established qualifier people already say (e.g. the ethnic qualifier of the official names 'Bambadinca Balanta' / 'Bambadinca Mancanha'), within the plate-name limit, decided once per name, listed in name-ranges.json summary.qualifiersNeeded; the qualified word is a name of its own

spotGrid.frame: per sector: SW corner of the box (0.001 deg), phi0, cell = longer side / 10000 rounded up to 0.1 m
spotGrid.refinement: 9th digit on the phone-keypad layout (1 2 3 north row) divides the cell by 3

validation.method: proximity rule re-run with enclosures hidden, compared with OpenStreetMap-mapped moranças and walled plots of 2+ footprints

spoken.source: 2009 census via Wikipedia, Languages of Guinea-Bissau

languages.howNumbersAreSaid: numbers up to 99 as one number; 4-digit numbers in two pairs ('doze, setenta e quatro') or digit by digit, as phone numbers are; the app's voice reads digit by digit

existingPostcodes.bissau: 1000 BISSAU printed as the postal line of every address in sector 10
existingPostcodes.elsewhere: locality name only, until Correios publishes codes; then mapped per sector/place

useClasses.residential.compound-house: casa de morança: the main rectangular house of a family compound (adobe or block, zinc or thatch roof)
useClasses.residential.round-house: palhota / casa redonda: round house, Bijagós, Balanta, Fula and Mandinka areas (only detectable on OpenStreetMap outlines)
useClasses.residential.annex: cozinha, celeiro, armazém, latrina beside a main house
useClasses.residential.house: single house (vivenda), mostly Bissau and towns
useClasses.commercial.market: mercado (Bandim, Caracol) and lumo (weekly market, east)
useClasses.government: ministry, sector administration, court, police, post office
useClasses.health: hospital, centro de saúde, posto sanitário, farmácia
useClasses.religious.shrine: baloba / sacred house: stored, not published without the community's agreement
useClasses.hospitality: hotel, pensão, restaurante, bar, Bijagós lodges
useClasses.mixed: home with a shop in the wall

buildingProfile.inference: engine/SPEC.md section 8.3: OSM tags 0.85-0.90; N-Ways places 0.65; enclosure kind 0.55; round shape 0.60; annex by size 0.45; large 0.30; default compound house 0.50-0.65
buildingProfile.height: OpenStreetMap height/building:levels only (82 buildings have levels). The ML parquet h is a rendering filler and is never used.

private: household composition (only a declared count, aggregate)
doors of a home on request
gate photos (kept for confirmation, not published)

headline.census2026: about 301,000 households and over 600,000 dwellings counted by 22 June 2026 (INE, preliminary): about 1.25 households per machine-grouped compound

steps: stand at the gate: GPS averaged 10-20 s + one gate photo
outline: tap corners on imagery, or walk the boundary with AR, or type/photograph survey beacons (state the datum: Bissau / UTM 28N EPSG:2095 or WGS 84 / UTM 28N EPSG:32628)
confirmed by arrivals/deliveries, no neighbour dispute, or new imagery
checks: AR and GPS tracks agree (< 8 m)
inside the n-ways or mixed coverage
addMyHome.notATitle: a code is an address, not a land title, concession or proof of rights (Lei da Terra 5/98: land is State property; customary use rights)
addMyHome.offline: spot code at once; compound code from the registry on next connection
addMyHome.cadastre: Direcção Geral de Geografia e Cadastro holds partial paper cadastre (Bissau, towns, concessions); no public parcel data; unverified detail

gettingYourCode.app: Your home code card as soon as home is saved or the phone stands at the gate: 0 taps to see, 2 taps to share (Share -> WhatsApp/SMS link)
gettingYourCode.plates: plate on the gate: big remembered form (BANDIM 275), the official name in small type when it differs, and a QR code holding the machine form
gettingYourCode.partners: couriers and partners look up a customer's code with the customer's consent
notNow: SMS lookup service (possible later option only)

governance: GOVERNANCE.md: N-WAYS LIMITED issues until the State designates a body; INE, Câmara Municipal de Bissau, Correios, DGGC, ARN-TIC; hand-over whole or Bissau alone

dataProtection.regional: ECOWAS Supplementary Act A/SA.1/01/10 (2010), under review
dataProtection.bill: Electronic Transactions Law, public consultation May 2026

rollout.fieldEvaluation: Bissau (Bandim, Bairro Militar, Cuntum) + one tabanca cluster in Biombo or Oio
rollout.memorabilityTest: recall after 1 week and 4 weeks; spoken/typed/written error rates; place-word+number vs digits-only vs alphanumeric
